deviations.commit: the commit that adds this entry
deviations.what: Three rule changes after the code review: (1) A0 = the cell winner with the best score on common targets, no 1-SE rule (the 1-SE rule still picks each cell's winner); (2) the D23 gate makes one comparison, against the shorter full-overlap length with the best R1 score, instead of against every shorter length; (3) each pre-registered comparison is scored on the samples both of its arms predict, replacing 'every arm from the latest first prediction of any final arm'; that shared start is kept for the descriptive scores and the val-test agreement (D2b). Adds 'limitations' (no shuffling vs overlap, fixed training settings, ridge lags, conservative rule). Considered and not adopted: drawing 1 or 2 layers in the fine round (fine draws keep the centre's layers).
deviations.why: (1) parameter count does not depend on window length, so the fewest-parameters tie-break ignored the setting being chosen and, with 6 people, many cells fall within 1 SE; (2) comparing against every shorter length made stopping more likely by multiplicity; (3) the old rule made F3's scored samples depend on F1's gate results and dropped up to 10 s of every trial from comparisons not involving long windows, while the descriptive curve and D2b need one shared sample set to line up. Layers stay fixed in the fine round because drawing them afresh would move most fine draws off the centre whose learning-rate and dropout ranges were narrowed, and the seed check already pools coarse and fine configs, so the other layer count stays in contention.

deviations.what: 6-day compute budget (user): coarse draws 8 -> 6 (+ anchor), fine draws 8 -> 4, final seeds per cell winner 5 -> 3 (A0, A2, A3 keep 10); 6 workers; only the 2 s window is screened and a pass is reported as 'not tuned (budget)' (5 s and 10 s are not screened); a run-time budget check, when the R1 runs of every cell but 75 % overlap end and again when R1 ends, adds, in order, drop the 75 % overlap cells (their R1 runs come after the first check), skip the 2 s check, fine draws 4 -> 2, until the projection is within 6 days (EXPERIMENTS/tuning/budget.py, results_v2/budget.json).
deviations.why: The full-budget design projected 8.2-8.7 days, and more if runs train past epoch 180; the user set a hard 6-day limit. The cuts keep every cell and every pre-registered comparison and were the shortening path listed in the plan. The fallback depends on run times only, never on scores. A lower epoch cap was considered as a fallback step and not adopted: applied mid-study it would give runs of the same round different training budgets. A 7th worker was not adopted (the M3 has 4 performance + 4 efficiency cores).

limitations: No shuffling (D27): with stride-1 windows in time order a batch of 64 is 0.64 s of one trial, while at 0 % overlap a batch spans 64 distinct windows; the overlap family (F2) therefore also measures batch diversity, and an overlap effect may partly be a shuffling effect.
Fixed, untuned training settings: ReduceLROnPlateau 0.5/6, early-stopping patience 15, clipnorm 1.0, dropout at most 0.3, no weight decay.
The lagged ridge baseline (A1) sees 0.5 s of lags, while the networks get up to 10 s of history: a reference, not an equal competitor.
The decision rule (all 6 people agree in sign and median effect >= 5 %) is conservative, so 'no clear difference' is the expected outcome for small effects.
